Request Info
The PhD in Civil Engineering prepares researchers who can define original problems in their field and solve them rigorously. Doctoral students complete advanced coursework in one of five areas of specialization, pass a comprehensive examination covering a major and two minor subject areas, defend a research proposal, and produce and defend a dissertation of original scholarship established by external peer review.
Request Info
Apply
Visit
At a Glance
Five Areas of Specialization: Candidates can choose between Construction Engineering and Management; Transportation and Systems Engineering; Structural Engineering; Environmental Engineering and Water Resource Management; and Civil Engineering Informatics.
Flexibility: The Civil Engineering PhD program offers daytime and evening courses, small doctoral cohorts, and the ability to work directly with faculty members. Up to 24 credits from Master's degrees earned elsewhere (or 30 from a Catholic University master's program) are transferable, substantially reducing time to degree.
Funding Opportunities: Teaching and research assistantships with stipend and tuition remission are available through the College.
Program Details
The doctorate is a research degree, and the structure reflects that: coursework establishes command of a field, the comprehensive examination tests it, and everything after is original work. Students are expected to be in continuous contact with their adviser throughout the research and writing.
Residence
Doctoral students enroll full-time — at least nine credit hours per semester — for a minimum of three semesters while completing coursework. Students who complete the minimum period of residence continue in extended residence until all requirements are met, registering for comprehensives or dissertation guidance unless granted a leave of absence. The minimum GPA for admission to doctoral study is 3.4.
Comprehensive Examination
The comprehensive examination covers the candidate’s major area together with two minor subject areas related to the intended research. It may be taken after all required coursework is complete, or during the semester in which the coursework will be finished; students register for ENGR 998A in the former case and ENGR 998B in the latter. A student who fails may sit the examination a second time; a second failure ends eligibility to continue toward the doctorate. Students advance to candidacy on completing the coursework and passing the examination.
Proposal, Dissertation, and Defense
The proposal defense establishes that the plan of research is complete and holds academic merit. The written proposal goes to every member of the doctoral committee at least two weeks before the defense and must demonstrate a complete literature review, preliminary results already obtained, and a clear plan of research with specific tasks and expected outcomes. The dissertation itself must present original research giving evidence of excellent, significant, and original scholarship as established by external peer review, and must be approved by the directing professor and the dissertation committee. The final defense is administered by the full committee — a minimum of three faculty members in addition to the chair and a secretary assigned by the College — and is primarily on the dissertation, though questions may be asked in the candidate’s major field.
After advancing to candidacy, students register for at least one dissertation guidance course (ENGR 996) every semester and must complete all requirements within five years.
Admission
Admission decisions are made by the College in consultation with the department, based on undergraduate and graduate transcripts, work experience and prior scholarly work, GRE scores, and at least three academic letters of recommendation. The minimum GPA for admission to doctoral study is 3.4. The GRE requirement may be waived where the College or department finds other evidence of a candidate’s proficiency, such as published work or professional experience. Non-native English speakers demonstrate proficiency through TOEFL scores or at least two years of study at an English-speaking institution.
Curriculum
The Doctor of Philosophy in Civil Engineering requires 53 credits.
Coursework Requirement (53 credits)
Three common core courses — 9 credits
Four required courses in the chosen area — 12 credits
Area electives — at least 32 credits (up to two ENGR 993 Directed Study courses, 6 credits total)
ENGR 998A or ENGR 998B in the semester of the comprehensive examination
ENGR 996 Dissertation Guidance every semester after advancement to candidacy
Courses and Electives
Common Core Courses
Doctoral students complete three of the following five common core courses:
ENGR 516 — Computational Methods in Engineering
ENGR 520 / ENGR 521 — Mathematical Analysis for Graduate Students / Partial Differential Equations
CEE / CMGT 575 — Introduction to Systems Analysis
CMGT 547 — Engineering Economics
ENGR 518 — Experimental Methods in Engineering
Additional core courses beyond the required number may be counted as area electives.
Required Courses by Area
Each area requires the four courses listed below. If a required course is not offered during a student’s period of study, another 500-level course may be substituted with the permission of the academic advisor or the graduate advising coordinator.

CEE 594 Construction Law, Operations and Project Delivery (alternating semesters)
CEE 542 Construction Field Operations (Spring)
CMGT 575 Introduction to Systems Analysis
Transportation and Systems Engineering
CEE 511 Geographical Information Systems
CEE 517 Multimodal Transportation Engineering (Fall)
CSC 530 Introduction to Data Analysis
Structural Engineering
CEE 514 / ME 514 Advanced Vibrations and Structural Dynamics (alternating semesters)
CEE 526 Introduction to Finite Elements (Fall)
CEE 506 Advanced Structural Systems (alternating semesters)
ENGR 518 Experimental Techniques for Graduate Students (Spring) or CEE 523 Structural Loads on Civil Structures
Environmental Engineering and Water Resource Management
CEE 597 Water and Wastewater Treatment Engineering (alternating semesters)
CEE 526 Introduction to Finite Elements or CEE 565 Water Resources Engineering (Fall)
CEE 563 Applied Hydrology (Fall) or CEE 591 Hydrogeology (alternating semesters)
CEE 564 Surface Water Quality (alternating semesters) or CEE 511 Geographical Information Systems
Civil Engineering Informatics
CEE 511 Geographical Information Systems
CSC 513 Fundamentals of Computer Graphics
Advanced Numerical Methods in Partial Differential Equations or CEE 526 Introduction to Finite Elements (Fall)
CSC 530 Introduction to Data Analysis

Transfer Credit
Up to 24 credits from a master’s program completed elsewhere, or up to 30 credits from a master’s program completed at Catholic University, may be applied toward the doctoral coursework requirement.
FAQs
How long does the PhD take?
It depends heavily on transfer credit and research progress. Students entering with a master’s degree may transfer up to 24 credits (30 if the master’s was earned at Catholic University), which greatly reduces remaining coursework. After advancement to candidacy, all requirements must be completed within five years.
Is funding available?
Teaching and research assistantships carrying a stipend and tuition remission are available through the College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing. Contact the department and submit the College’s graduate TA/RA application materials.
Is the GRE required?
Yes for doctoral applicants, and GRE scores are necessary to be considered for most university scholarships. The requirement may be waived where the College or department finds other evidence of proficiency, such as published work or substantial professional experience.
What does the comprehensive examination cover?
Your major area plus two minor subject areas related to your intended research. You may take it after finishing all required coursework or during the semester you will finish, registering for ENGR 998A or ENGR 998B accordingly. It may be retaken once.
Do I need a master’s degree to apply?
No, though many students enter with one. Applicants are evaluated on transcripts, work experience and prior scholarly work, GRE scores, and at least three academic letters of recommendation, with a minimum GPA of 3.4 for admission to doctoral study.
Can I study part-time?
Coursework requires full-time enrollment of at least nine credits per semester for a minimum of three semesters. Courses run in a mix of daytime and evening sections, but the residence requirement means the doctorate is not a part-time-only degree.
